failures.claim: In the current period, reputational and client franchise risk was flagged as changed since the prior period due to increased external scrutiny and engagement activity; flood exposure risk and stranded assets risk were not flagged as changed.

Scenario resilience assessment under orderly transition scenarios indicates green loan growth and client engagement on transition plans are expected to progressively reduce high-carbon sector concentration over the medium term.

Under orderly transition scenarios (short to medium term), the portfolio demonstrates adequate resilience; monitored through internal capital and risk metrics; Pillar 2 buffer thresholds are not disclosed in this section.

Under disorderly transition scenarios, near-term resilience is acceptable but medium-term capital consumption from stranded asset impairments is material; additional capital buffers may be required post-2030 under the most adverse disorderly assumptions.

For hot house world scenarios (long term), physical risk losses are identified as the dominant long-term resilience challenge via flood-exposed mortgage collateral revaluation risk and agricultural borrower default risk from chronic heat stress; resilience mechanisms for the 2050 horizon include a flood-zone overlay and EPC-based collateral monitoring.
Financed emissions for 2024 are reported as 35,973,167.6878965 tCO2e.
As at 2024, target progress is reported as: Scope 1 and 2 progress 40.0%, Scope 3 Category 15 progress 25.0%, and net zero progress (all scopes) 13.3%.
A portfolio intensity target of 20.0 tCO2e per EUR million is disclosed and monitored as part of portfolio decarbonisation glide-path monitoring.

Planned funding sources for the climate strategy include operating cash flows, capital allocation within annual budgeting and multi-year strategic plan, and client-linked financing activity.
As at 2024, target progress is reported as: Scope 1 and 2 progress 40.0%, Scope 3 Category 15 progress 25.0%, and net zero progress (all scopes) 13.3%.
